Vote-by-mail (absentee voting) is available in Maine and no excuse is required. The last day to request an absentee ballot is the Thursday before every election at 5:00pm. You can submit your absentee ballot request form through the mail, by email, in person at your local elections office, or online (https://apps.web.maine.gov/cgi-bin/online/AbsenteeBallot/index.pl).

Voted ballots must be received by 8:00pm on Election Day to be counted. You can track your absentee ballot on the Secretary of State's website (https://apps.web.maine.gov/cgi-bin/online/AbsenteeBallot/ballot_status.pl).

For information on federal campaign contributions, please visit Open Secrets (http://www.opensecrets.org).

For information on state campaign contributions, please visit your state's resource. (https://mainecampaignfinance.com/#/index)

Local election information is collected by League volunteers and may not be complete. If you don't see your local ballot, you may still have an election - please contact your town clerk

Information on local, state and federal candidates and ballot measures may be available here (https://www.vote411.org/ballot#.UFoDEFHh-Sp).
Ballot curing is when a voter corrects an issue with their ballot, so it can be counted.

Early voting for the November 3, 2026 General Election begins on October 5th and ends on October 29th.

Early Voting (in-person absentee voting) Starts: 30 days before Election Day

Early Voting (in-person absentee voting) Ends: 3 business days before Election Day

The next election date can be found here https://www.vote411.org/maine.

Contact your local Board of Elections (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm) for more information.

All polls open between 6am and 10am until 8pm.

You can find your polling place by utilizing your state resource. (https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.maine.gov%2Fportal%2Fgovernment%2Fedemocracy%2Fvoter_lookup.php&data=05%7C01%7CMBrown%40lwv.org%7C6e9a2edef3324b0bd44f08da967888c9%7C90befbfe6dce4edfba8a35fb67131124%7C1%7C0%7C637987741685084629%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=yS%2Br%2FTrAL5kZaOZjAEeGjb%2BNPH5dGh4%2FJuQ28LC5nEY%3D&reserved=0)

If you have further questions on your polling place location, please contact your Municipal Clerk (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

Maine overseas citizens and U.S. military personnel can register to vote and request an absentee ballot on the Maine Secretary of State’s website.  (https://www.maine.gov/sos/elections-voting/uniformed-service-and-overseas-voters)

You can find your polling place by utilizing your state resource. (http://www.maine.gov/portal/government/edemocracy/voter_lookup.php)

If you have further questions on your polling place location, please contact your M (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)unicipal Clerk (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

Maine now has semi-open primaries. If you are registered with a political party, you can only vote in that party’s primary. If you are not registered with a political party (unenrolled), you can choose which party’s primary to vote in. You may only vote in one party’s primary.

This applies to both presidential and state primaries.

If you want to change your party affiliation, you must do so at least 15 days before Election Day.

Ranked Choice Voting (RCV)

Maine uses a ranked choice voting system for Presidential Primaries, State Primaries, and General Elections. To find out more about ranked choice voting click here (https://www.vote411.org/maine#ranked-choice-voting).

If you have any questions about your state’s primary election, please contact your local election officials (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

Maine allows voters to vote using Ranked Choice Voting (https://www.lwvme.org/RCVhelp) for all state-level primary elections, and in general elections ONLY for federal offices, including the office of U.S. President. Ranked choice voting allows voters to rank the candidates in the order of their preference.
